name: Chi Protocol ArbitrageV5 burn gated on manipulable USC spot price
summary: ArbitrageV5.burn() redeems USC from the reserve holder at a hard-coded $1, gated only by the USC/WETH Uniswap V2 spot price being within maxMintBurnPriceDiff ($0.50) of peg and by a reserve-deficit check. With USC trading near $0.0005 in a pool holding 0.005 WETH, the attacker bought 17,343 USC for 0.158 flash-loaned WETH, lifting the spot to about $0.50, deposited 3.9 WETH into the reserve holder to pass the deficit check, burned the USC for 1.71 weETH, 2.82 stETH and its 3.9 WETH back, and sold the rest.
notes: Reset is the reserve holder's setArbitrager(ArbitrageV5, true) (isArbitrager mapping, slot 105), which let burn() redeem reserves; ArbitrageV5 was deployed 7 days earlier. Later owner changes only resized the gate: maxMintBurnPriceDiff $0.05 to $0.50, per-call burn limits to 5M USC, and maxMintBurnReserveTolerance 1% to 100%; a larger purchase, more burn calls or a larger deposit pass the old values (rule 8).

The seven burns since block 23686246 ran at unmanipulated spot prices of $0.59-0.97. USC collapsed after an unrelated stUSC self-transfer inflation dumped 16,949 USC into the pool 20 hours before (0x706158ec, separate defect). Loss is the reserve vaults' outflow; the attacker's 3.9 WETH deposit nets out (rule 11) and the pool's USC is worthless (rule 12).
